title: Defects found in the 1.3.0 merge review (verified in code)
description: Cheap, independent fixes that must land before the daemon becomes more central; each is one commit on its own fix/<slug> branch from origin/main, test shown failing first. Found by the 2026-10-08 external review of SUGGESTIONS-vcache-daemon.md and verified against the code.

title: rustc identity memo is keyed on path and size only; a same-size relink reuses the old banner
description: ResolveRustcFingerprint keys rustc-version-memo-v1 on realpath + size. ResolveCompilerId (C++) adds mtime and its comment explains why: relinking a compiler after a source change routinely lands on the same byte count. Add mtime, bump the memo name to v2. Fails first: a unit test that rewrites the fake rustc with same-size different bytes and a newer mtime and expects a new fingerprint.

title: util::ReadFile reads through istreambuf_iterator: 28% of vcache CPU on a warm build
description: perf on a warm 357-crate build: ReadFile 28%, BLAKE3 17%, memmove 9% of vcache's own CPU, which is 82% of all CPU in that build; the 550 MB asupersync entry takes 1.7 s to serve. Replace with fstat + a single read into a presized string (or mmap for blobs above a threshold) and remove the extra copies in DeserializeBlob/RestoreOutputs where a string_view suffices. Fails first: none applicable (no behaviour change); record the before/after warm wall time and perf share in the commit body instead.

title: Queued S3 upload is skipped when the disk layer evicts the entry first
description: UploadWorker re-reads the blob from disk; if DiskStorage::Put's inline LRU eviction removed it, the upload is counted as uploads_skipped and lost. Under cache pressure the newest entries are evicted first, so S3 silently loses exactly the latest work. Fix: the evictor skips keys with a pending/<key> journal marker (the journal is already the pin list). Fails first: an integration test with a tiny disk size and a mock S3 showing uploads_skipped stays 0.

title: Server::Enqueue dedupes by key, so a manifest re-Put is absorbed by an in-flight upload of the old value
description: queued_keys_ makes a second Put of the same key a no-op while the first upload is pending; manifests are mutable, so the newer states never reach S3. Fix: generation-aware enqueue (requeue when the value changed) or re-read the disk value at upload time and loop while it changed. Fails first: a unit test that two Puts of one key with different values end with the second value uploaded.

title: RestoreOutputs joins stored file names onto the output dir without a traversal check
description: A blob file name containing '..' escapes parsed.out_dir on a hit. Harmless with a single-user disk cache; material once blobs come from S3 or a peer. Reject names with '..' components or an absolute path at restore and at capture. Fails first: a unit test that a crafted blob is refused.

title: held_ hits are reported to the client as layer disk
description: HandleGet serves a blob from held_ (awaiting upload, disk layer absent) and labels the reply "disk", so the client counts kHitDisk while the daemon counts hits_memory. Report "memory" and count it on the client. Fails first: an integration test with disk disabled and a mock S3 that checks --show-stats after a held_ hit.

title: Concurrent LoadManifest/StoreManifest cycles lose each other's states
description: Two compiles of one manifest key in different worktrees read the same states, each prepends its own and writes back; the second write drops the first's state. Merge on store (re-read, union by key, cap) instead of overwrite. Fails first: a unit test that two interleaved store cycles leave both states present.

title: Daemon as scheduler: single-flight keys, memory-aware admission, jobserver pool
description:
Make the 1.3.0 daemon the machine-wide coordinator for every build that goes through vcache: deduplicate in-flight compiles of one key across worktrees, admit compiles by memory (estimate from the prior compile or link of the same cost key, against MemAvailable minus what in-flight compiles are still going to take), and own a GNU-make-style fifo jobserver that ninja 1.13+, make 4.4+ and cargo/rustc draw job slots from.

Proposal as filed upstream: Unto-Labs/vcache issue (see the epic's external ref). Background and the rejected alternatives: SUGGESTIONS-vcache-daemon.md v2 (session scratchpad, 2026-10-08), sections 3 (ground rules), 4 (defects) and tiers B/C.

Workflow for every child: branch `feat/<slug>` from origin/main (our integration branch = upstream 1.3.0 + fork fixes, 499 unit / 379 integration checks green), `make test` with MAKEFLAGS=-j8 and ccache off PATH, every new check shown failing first (AGENTS.md), push the branch, merge --no-ff into main, push main. Changes to the shipped binary end the commit body with `Deploy: vcache`; rebuild dist/ with devtools' host-setup-buildcache.sh --force after the merge. Do not touch the sibling repos' vcache-env.sh from these beads; the ninja/cargo integration bead files the follow-ups there.

Ordering: rusage capture first (everything else reads its cost records), then single-flight and admission (independent of each other), then jobserver mode (needs admission's memory view), then the build-tool integration and the measurement bead last.

title: Record each compile's and link's peak RSS and wall time (wait4) in the blob meta and a cost table
description:
util::Run waits with waitpid and discards resource usage. Switch to wait4 and surface ru_maxrss (KiB) and wall time in ProcResult. For the clang/gcc driver, wait4's ru_maxrss is the largest waited-for child's peak, i.e. cc1plus; rustc is single-process; a link is the linker itself. Record them: (a) in the blob's meta string on store ("maxrss_kb:", "wall_ms:"), (b) in a daemon-side cost table keyed by a cost key = canonical source path + language + codegen flag class (content excluded), persisted under <cache>/costs/ and loaded lazily, with a fallback default per (language, operation). Expose both through VCACHE_LOG lines and a `--show-costs` summary (count, p50, max per operation).

Fails first: a unit test that the cost key ignores content and roots but not the flag class; an integration test that a compile's recorded maxrss is non-zero and its wall time within the measured run. No behaviour change for lookups yet.

title: Single-flight: kAcquire/kRelease lease per key so concurrent worktrees compile a miss once
description:
New daemon ops kAcquire(key) -> granted | wait(holder cost estimate) and kRelease(key, outcome). The first client past key computation holds the key; later clients wait for the holder's kPut (HandlePut wakes waiters) and then kGet. Lease rules, all required: memory-only (never journalled, dropped on daemon restart with waiters told to compile), a renewable TTL over a dedicated held connection (RoundTrip's one-connection-per-request stays for everything else), expiry on socket close or missed renewal, a failed holder compile releases and waiters compile, waiters bound their wait by max(holder's recorded wall time x2, 30 s) because a waiting wrapper still holds a ninja/cargo job slot, Shutdown must not wait on lease connections, and a speculative or read-only client never holds. Wire the acquire into RunCompile, RunRustCompile and RunLink between the key and the compile, and coalesce concurrent S3 GETs of one key through the same table. --daemon-status gains held/waiting counts.

Fails first: an integration test with two trees that miss on one key under VCACHE_DAEMON=auto showing one "rust compile:"/"compile:" log line and two hits; a unit test that a dead holder's lease expires and the waiter is told to compile; a test that a failing holder releases.

title: Memory-aware admission: kReserve against MemAvailable minus unrealised in-flight reservations
description:
Before running the compiler on a miss (and the linker), the client asks kReserve(cost_key, estimate_kb, compiler_pid once spawned). The daemon grants when MemAvailable (/proc/meminfo, refreshed at most once per second) minus the unrealised part of outstanding reservations covers the estimate. Unrealised_i = max(0, estimate_i - current RSS_i), with RSS sampled from /proc/<pid>/status of the reported compiler pids every 500 ms; v1 may instead subtract the whole estimate for the first 10 s of each compile. FIFO queue of waiters; always at least one compile in flight so an estimate above the machine cannot deadlock; a reservation dies with the client's held connection; VCACHE_DAEMON off or a refused client means no admission (today's behaviour). Estimates come from the cost table (sibling bead); without one, a per-(language, operation) default from config (daemon.default_compile_kb, daemon.default_link_kb). --daemon-status gains reserved / realised / waiting rows; VCACHE_LOG records each wait and its length.

Fails first: a unit test of the admission arithmetic (grant, refuse, release, the always-one rule, realised RSS reducing the unrealised sum); an integration test with a fake /proc/meminfo path (daemon.meminfo_path, test-only) showing a second compile waits until the first releases.

title: Jobserver mode: the daemon owns a fifo job-slot pool that ninja, make and cargo draw from
description:
daemon.jobserver = true (or --jobserver-jobs N) makes the daemon create <state dir>/jobserver.fifo and write N tokens (default: online CPUs). `vcache --jobserver-env` prints `MAKEFLAGS=-j --jobserver-auth=fifo:<path>` for builds to export; ninja 1.13+ follows it when no -j is given (POSIX fifo form only), GNU make 4.4+ and cargo/rustc via the jobserver crate too. The pool is elastic: under memory pressure (the admission bead's view) the daemon reads free tokens back out of the fifo and writes them back when MemAvailable recovers; a token held by a running job is never touched. --stop-daemon removes the fifo; --daemon-status shows tokens total / free / withdrawn. Document in docs/daemon.md with the ninja/make/cargo version requirements and that -l load limits still apply.

Fails first: a unit test of the token-withdraw/restore arithmetic; an integration test that `make -j` and a tiny ninja file under the exported MAKEFLAGS run no more than N jobs concurrently (a sleeping fake compiler counts its peers through a shared counter file) and that withdrawing tokens lowers the ceiling.

title: Build-tool integration: sibling build scripts export the daemon's MAKEFLAGS instead of computing -j
description: Follow-up outside this repo once the jobserver bead ships: devtools' vcache-env.sh gains an opt-in (FBG_VCACHE_JOBSERVER=1) that starts the daemon with jobserver mode and exports its MAKEFLAGS; sunbird's build.sh stops passing -j to ninja when that is set (its start-of-build MemAvailable snapshot is exactly the gap the daemon closes); cargo picks the fifo up from MAKEFLAGS. Verify cargo 1.97 and rustc actually take tokens from a fifo jobserver (strace one build) before switching sunbird. Record the before/after in the measurement bead. This bead only files the devtools and sunbird beads with the exact env contract; it is closed when those exist.

title: Measure: two and three concurrent worktree builds with and without single-flight, admission and the jobserver
description: On the 128-core / 125 GB host: Rust workspace (357 crates; today 4-5 s warm, 115 s cold per worktree) and the C++ tree (~400 TUs) in 2 and 3 worktrees started together. Record wall time per build, the minimum MemAvailable during the run (sample /proc/meminfo at 1 Hz), OOM-killer events (dmesg), duplicate compiles avoided (--daemon-status) and admission waits (VCACHE_LOG). Compare daemon off, single-flight only, +admission, +jobserver. Write the table into docs/daemon.md and post the numbers on the upstream proposal issue. Keep usernames, hostnames and repo names out of anything posted upstream.
